channel.title: Majorca Daily Bulletin - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Majorca Daily Bulletin (majorcadailybulletin.com)

item.title: It’s official: Spain has been a total washout since October! Weather patterns becoming more ‘dangerous disasters’
item.description: Climate change has increased the intensity of torrential rains that caused flooding in Spain, Portugal and northern Morocco, according to an analysis by the international scientific group World Weather Attribution (WWA).

item.title: Aldi expands in the Balearics with new stores set to open in Mallorca
item.description: Aldi plans to hire 163 employees in the Balearic Islands in 2026, boosting its workforce by 62% and reinforcing its presence across Mallorca, Menorca and Ibiza.

item.title: Balearics does not want any more tourists this summer: 70% of hotels to open in March
item.description: Last year air traffic achieved a new record with 23.6 million passengers, an increase of 1.3% year-on-year, while maritime traffic fell by 1.1%

item.title: Balearic Government rejects Mallorca town’s move to cap housing prices
item.description: Esporles’ self-declaration as a tensioned zone carries symbolic weight but does not compel the Government to impose price limits.

item.title: The Mallorca few remember: what the island was like in the summers of the 1970s
item.description: The footage combines images of packed beaches, bustling hotels and streets filled with visitors enjoying shopping, dining outdoors and sightseeing.

item.title: Woman locked in hotel room and robbed of €3,000 at taser point in Mallorca
item.description: The investigation began after the woman filed a complaint in December.

item.title: Mallorca events: What's On from Friday, 27 February to Thursday, 5 March
item.description: This week in Mallorca, there’s plenty to see and do across Palma and the surrounding towns. From Friday, February 27, celebrate Balearics Day with food, music, and local culture at Sa Feixina Park, the Cathedral, and beyond, while enjoying live performances, guided tours, and family-friendly activities. From baroque piano recitals and folk dances to food trucks and wine tastings, there’s something for everyone, plus special events running through the weekend and into next week across Palma, Inca

item.title: Palma to cut cruise ship numbers in summer under new deal
item.description: The agreement maintains a cap of three cruise ships per day in Palma’s port.

item.title: Fundación Calvià 365 and El Corte Inglés join forces to sponsor Calvia’s major sporting events
item.description: The deal encompasses three high-profile events: the Galatzó Trail, the Half Marathon Magaluf and the Challenge Peguera Mallorca triathlon.

item.title: Mallorca weather for Saturday, February 28
item.description: Breezier on Saturday than over the past several days.
